Contents 1 The nature and objectives of the game of chess 2 Setup 3 The moves of the pieces 3.1 Promotion 3.2 Check 4 Game end 5 Variant: Chess960 5.1 Starting position 5.2 Chess960 castling rules 5.2.1 Clarification 5.2.1.1 c-side castling 5.2.1.2 g-side castling 6 Glossary of terms in the Laws of Chess The nature and objectives of the game of chess The game of chess is played between two opponents who move their pieces on a square board. The player with the light-coloured pieces (White) makes the first move, then the players move alternately, with the player with the dark-coloured pieces (Black) making the next move. The objective of each player is to place the opponent’s king ‘under attack’ in such a way that the opponent has no legal move. The player who achieves this goal is said to have ‘checkmated’ the opponent’s king and has won the game. The following are not allowed: leaving one’s own king under attack, exposing one’s own king to attack, moving one's king over a threatened square. If the position is such that neither player can possibly checkmate the opponent’s king, the game is drawn (either by "stalemate", if no legal move is possible, or by "insufficient material"). The moves of the pieces It is not permitted to move a piece to a square occupied by a piece of the same colour. If a piece moves to a square occupied by an opponent’s piece the latter is captured and removed from the chessboard as part of the same move. A piece is said to attack an opponent’s piece if the piece could make a capture on that square. A piece is considered to attack a square even if this piece is constrained from moving to that square because it would then leave or place the king of its own colour under attack. Only knights may move over any intervening pieces. Bishop The bishop may move to any square along a diagonal on which it stands. [Rating: 1/10] This game would be fine if there weren't done studies on opening, which people just try to know by heart.

[Rating: 1/10] Chess would be a good game if there wasn't so many bloody books and articles written about how to play!  You can't just sit down with someone and play chess, 'cos chances are that they know a pile of 'opening gambits' and just thrash you at it.  You can't beat them by being clever or witty, you need to read books about chess!  Chess has ceased to be a game, it's just a contest about how much stuff you can remember about how to counter opening moves etc.  If only none of the literature about chess exested, I would probably feel inclinded to rate is 7 or 8 out of 10.

[Rating: 1/10] [Everyday fellow]: 'Hello. I love games, strategy games'   [Cretin]: 'Oh, me too. Let's play chess. I'm in the local club, and normally play for money. My ranking is.. blah blah.. and my favourite opening is the Modified Schlapper-Kipper.. blah blah..'   [Fellow]: 'Wait a mo... just loading my shotgun... now.. let me put this in yer mouth'  Chess is vaguely sinister - the black and white board and the ability to mate with horses reminds me of twisted masonic ceremonies. Yeah.. ask any Grandmaster....

[Rating: 1/10] I don't like thinking while playing, I like to talk. This really ruins the whole chess thing for me, besides I don't find thinking all that fun or I'd go to school more

[Rating: 1/10] Abstract, eternal, boring and computationally almost predictable. Its only positive feature is a set of rules which works well (not true for many modern boardgames...), but in 500 years you can do better.

[Rating: 1/10] The game I should love, but I have nothing good to say about.  I don't want to put in the effort to play this well when I do.  Unexplained hatred.

[Rating: 1/10] I hate this game. There is no chance. It is often touted as the basis for strategy, like if you can't win this one then you're a bad strategist. I can win other games but not this one. I never win. I am the worst chess player I know. Objectively, it is a good game but I must give it a one on the principal that this game always pisses me off.

[Rating: 1/10] I am finished with chess.  The game is no longer the one I knew in my youth.  I have a love/hate relationship with chess and right now:  Enjoying it for the first time in 6 years.   Plan to play at least one tournament this year.  I used to play tournaments years ago, but have not done so since 1998.  From about 1988-98 I played a lot of chess :)  Now, I'm on to other games, but I still play a game or two (mostly blitz) from time to time.  Classic game which teaches so much in so little time.  Since I've started recording games on the geek: 1660-1088=102.      Update: finally played a tourname

[Rating: 1/10] I absolutely despise this game. I mean, mechanically there doesn't seem to be anything wrong with it (although I suppose it's potentially solvable with hypothetical computing breakthroughs) but I never get an ounce of enjoyment out of it. For me it's just an exercise in paranoia.
